title: Add per-video noir mode override settings
description: Implement per-video Noir Mode settings after the core preset/rule model exists. Users/admins must be able to set a noir mode for a specific Jellyfin movie, episode, or video item once the plugin is installed. This is server-side state, so it works for any Jellyfin client when that playback uses server-side transcoding. The per-video setting defaults to disabled for every video. A missing item override is treated as disabled and must leave playback unchanged. The setting should be stored as an item override keyed by Jellyfin item ID and, where useful for wrapper matching, normalized media path. Supported states: disabled/no override, explicitly off, or specific preset ID. The override is the only way the MVP applies Noir Mode; there is no plugin-wide default, library default, collection default, or user default. Add API endpoints for item search and override CRUD: GET /NoirMode/items/search?query=..., GET /NoirMode/items/{itemId}/override, PUT /NoirMode/items/{itemId}/override, DELETE /NoirMode/items/{itemId}/override. Add an admin UI management view where admins can search videos, inspect current override state, and set disabled/off/preset. If Jellyfin exposes a safe item-detail action or metadata page hook, add that as a later convenience enhancement, but the searchable admin management view is the MVP.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can search for a Jellyfin video item, see that its Noir Mode setting is disabled by default, set it to off or a specific preset, save the override, remove the override, and see that NoirRuleService applies Noir Mode only for videos with preset overrides. Missing overrides are resolved as disabled. The wrapper-readable state export includes item overrides, and tests cover disabled/off/preset behavior.
close_reason: MVP implementation completed: buildable Jellyfin 10.11/net9 plugin, native wrapper, per-video disabled-by-default overrides, safe FFmpeg injection/pass-through behavior, admin APIs/page, diagnostics, ADR, integration harness docs, packaging script, release manifest, and 20 passing tests.

title: Build automated unit and process test suite

Create the automated test suite for the plugin services and wrapper. These tests should run without a full Jellyfin server where possible.

Required coverage:
- PluginConfiguration serialization/deserialization.
- NoirPresetService allowlist validation.
- NoirRuleService per-video override behavior and no-override disabled behavior.
- Wrapper state file read/parse behavior.

- NoirFilterInjector behavior for -vf, no -vf, stream copy, -filter_complex, disabled mode, invalid preset, and quoted paths.

Tests should be fast enough for normal local development and CI.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/process tests cover all listed service and wrapper branches, prove videos without overrides remain normal, and can be run with one documented dotnet test command.
close_reason: MVP implementation completed: buildable Jellyfin 10.11/net9 plugin, native wrapper, per-video disabled-by-default overrides, safe FFmpeg injection/pass-through behavior, admin APIs/page, diagnostics, ADR, integration harness docs, packaging script, release manifest, and 20 passing tests.

title: Build native FFmpeg wrapper pass-through executable
description:
Build the wrapper as a native .NET console executable that can be configured as Jellyfin's FFmpeg path. The first implementation must be strict pass-through: it accepts all arguments from Jellyfin, invokes the real FFmpeg binary with the exact same argument list, and preserves FFmpeg's exit code/stdout/stderr behavior.

Requirements:
- Support Windows and Linux publish targets.
- Accept configuration for the real FFmpeg path and noir state file path.
- Never overwrite or rename the real FFmpeg binary.
- Preserve argument boundaries exactly; do not join arguments into a single shell string.
- Return the real FFmpeg process exit code.
- Stream stdout/stderr in a way Jellyfin logs still capture useful output.
- Add clear error messages when the real FFmpeg path is missing or invalid.
acceptance_criteria: Wrapper pass-through can run a sample ffmpeg command on Windows/Linux without changing behavior, preserves exit codes, and has unit/process tests for argument forwarding and missing real-FFmpeg errors.
close_reason: MVP implementation completed: buildable Jellyfin 10.11/net9 plugin, native wrapper, per-video disabled-by-default overrides, safe FFmpeg injection/pass-through behavior, admin APIs/page, diagnostics, ADR, integration harness docs, packaging script, release manifest, and 20 passing tests.

title: Implement safe FFmpeg argument parsing and noir filter injection
description:
Implement the wrapper logic that parses Jellyfin FFmpeg arguments and injects the selected noir filter only when safe. This is the core playback behavior.

Injection rules:
- If noir is disabled or no matching rule exists, pass through unchanged.
- Identify the primary input from -i where possible and use the exported noir state to resolve the preset.
- If -vf exists, append the allowlisted noir filter with a comma.
- If no -vf exists, insert -vf <filter> before the output path.
- If video codec is stream copy, either replace video copy with a configured encoder only if that behavior is explicitly implemented and tested, or skip with a clear log message.
- If -filter_complex exists, skip injection in the MVP and log why.
- Preserve audio, subtitle, mapping, bitrate, HLS, and output arguments.
- Never accept arbitrary filter strings from request data; only use allowlisted presets from state.
acceptance_criteria: Argument parser and injector tests cover existing -vf, no -vf, stream copy, -filter_complex, disabled mode, invalid preset, quoted paths, Windows path arguments, and output path preservation. Unsupported commands pass through unchanged with logs.
close_reason: MVP implementation completed: buildable Jellyfin 10.11/net9 plugin, native wrapper, per-video disabled-by-default overrides, safe FFmpeg injection/pass-through behavior, admin APIs/page, diagnostics, ADR, integration harness docs, packaging script, release manifest, and 20 passing tests.

title: Implement wrapper install, status, and test API endpoints
description:
Implement plugin API endpoints that let the admin configure and validate the FFmpeg wrapper workflow. The plugin should detect the current Jellyfin FFmpeg path, save it as RealFFmpegPath, expose the expected wrapper path, and provide setup instructions if Jellyfin settings cannot be updated safely through a public API.

Suggested endpoints:
- GET /NoirMode/config
- POST /NoirMode/config
- GET /NoirMode/presets
- GET /NoirMode/wrapper/status
- POST /NoirMode/wrapper/install
- POST /NoirMode/wrapper/test
- GET /NoirMode/resolve?itemId=...

Status response should report: enabled state, real FFmpeg path, wrapper path, whether the wrapper exists, whether the real FFmpeg path is valid, state file freshness, and whether Jellyfin appears to be using the wrapper if that can be detected.
acceptance_criteria: Admin APIs validate input, persist settings, report wrapper status, expose preset data, and return actionable error messages with problem/cause/fix details. Endpoint tests cover success and failure cases.
close_reason: MVP implementation completed: buildable Jellyfin 10.11/net9 plugin, native wrapper, per-video disabled-by-default overrides, safe FFmpeg injection/pass-through behavior, admin APIs/page, diagnostics, ADR, integration harness docs, packaging script, release manifest, and 20 passing tests.

title: Build Jellyfin admin configuration page
description:
Build the Jellyfin plugin admin page for Noir Mode. The page is the universal configuration surface because most Jellyfin clients cannot show plugin-specific player controls. The admin page must not expose a server-wide default noir preset; Noir Mode is configured per video only.

Required controls:
- Plugin Enabled toggle for wrapper/admin features.
- Preset list/preview showing built-in preset labels and FFmpeg filter details, not arbitrary editable filters.
- Searchable item overrides management view for selecting videos and setting normal/off/specific preset.
- Wrapper status panel showing configured real FFmpeg path, wrapper path, state file freshness, and setup status.
- Wrapper install/test actions.
- Warnings that Direct Play/Direct Stream bypass FFmpeg and that hardware acceleration/subtitle burn-in may skip noir mode in the MVP.

Avoid exposing custom FFmpeg filter editing in the MVP.
acceptance_criteria: Admin page can load/save config, manage per-video overrides, show wrapper diagnostics, run wrapper test actions, and display clear warnings for Direct Play and unsupported transcoding paths. There is no default noir mode selector.

title: Implement plugin configuration and built-in noir presets
description:
Implement the persistent plugin configuration and built-in preset registry. The configuration must not include a full-server default noir preset. Noir Mode is opt-in per video: videos without item overrides play normally.

Required configuration fields:
- Enabled: plugin/wrapper/admin feature on/off flag, default false.
- AllowCustomFilters: default false.
- ForceTranscodeNoticeShown: default false.
- RealFFmpegPath: original Jellyfin FFmpeg path.
- WrapperPath: configured wrapper path.
- Presets: built-in and later custom preset definitions.
- ItemOverrides: per-video override records keyed by Jellyfin item ID and, where useful for wrapper matching, normalized media path.

Built-in presets:
- classic-bw: hue=s=0
- film-noir: hue=s=0,eq=contrast=1.35:brightness=-0.03
- high-contrast: hue=s=0,eq=contrast=1.6:brightness=-0.06
- vintage-noir: hue=s=0,eq=contrast=1.25:brightness=-0.02,noise=alls=12:allf=t+u
- soft-noir: hue=s=0,eq=contrast=1.15:brightness=0.01

Do not enable arbitrary custom filters in the MVP. Preset filter strings must come from an allowlisted registry.
acceptance_criteria: Configuration serializes/deserializes correctly, built-in presets resolve by ID, invalid preset IDs are rejected, no server-wide DefaultPresetId or ApplyDefaultWhenClientCannotSelect setting exists, and unit tests cover preset validation plus the no-override-means-normal behavior.

title: Implement noir rule resolution and wrapper-readable state export
description:
Implement the server-side rule service that decides whether a specific video item has a Noir Mode preset override. The service is the source of truth for clients that cannot choose a mode in their player. The MVP must not apply Noir Mode globally or through library/collection/user defaults.

Required precedence:
1. Optional temporary Jellyfin Web selection for the current video, if implemented.
2. Per-video item override.
3. Disabled: play the video normally.

Because the FFmpeg wrapper may not have authenticated Jellyfin context, export a wrapper-readable state file from the plugin. The state file should contain only the minimum data needed by the wrapper: enabled flag, preset allowlist, item overrides that can be matched by media path/item ID if available, and a generated version/timestamp. Store it in the plugin data directory with restrictive permissions where possible.
acceptance_criteria: NoirRuleService returns the expected preset for per-video overrides, returns disabled for videos without overrides, supports explicit off/normal behavior, exports item override state atomically, and tests cover the per-video-only precedence.
close_reason: MVP implementation completed: buildable Jellyfin 10.11/net9 plugin, native wrapper, per-video disabled-by-default overrides, safe FFmpeg injection/pass-through behavior, admin APIs/page, diagnostics, ADR, integration harness docs, packaging script, release manifest, and 20 passing tests.

title: Implement Jellyfin Noir Mode plugin MVP
description: Implement the Jellyfin Noir Mode plugin described in plugin-plan.md. The MVP must be GPLv3, use a standard Jellyfin plugin for configuration/API/admin UI, and use a native FFmpeg wrapper executable to inject allowlisted noir FFmpeg filters during server-side video transcoding. The core compatibility contract is: Noir Mode works on any Jellyfin client when playback uses Jellyfin server-side video transcoding. Direct Play and Direct Stream bypass FFmpeg and are not guaranteed until a later force-transcode research task proves a safe path. Noir Mode is opt-in per video only: videos without an item override play normally, and there is no full-server default noir preset. Optional Jellyfin Web controls can be added after the server-side per-video path works, but they are not the universal control plane.
acceptance_criteria: Epic is complete when the plugin can be installed on a supported Jellyfin server, configured through the admin UI, use a wrapper as Jellyfin's FFmpeg path, apply built-in noir presets during simple transcoding only for videos with item overrides, pass through videos without overrides unchanged, pass through unsupported commands safely, and ship with tests and packaging docs.

title: Research force-transcode feasibility and Jellyfin core hook path
description:
Research whether a plugin can safely force video transcoding for all clients or whether this requires Jellyfin core changes. This task exists because Noir Mode cannot affect Direct Play or Direct Stream, and the project must not claim universal all-playback support without proof.

Research questions:
- Is there any public Jellyfin plugin API that can modify PlaybackInfo, media source selection, client profiles, or transcoding decisions before playback starts?
- Can server-side settings reliably force transcode without client-specific setup?
- Is a core patch needed to add an ITranscodingFilterProvider-style extension point?
- What is the least invasive upstreamable design for a transcode filter provider?
- What are the risks of spoofing profiles or manipulating client requests?

Deliverable should be an ADR or plan update with a clear yes/no answer for plugin-only force-transcode support.
acceptance_criteria: Research produces a documented decision: plugin-only force-transcode is supported with implementation details, or it is not supported and requires a Jellyfin core patch/fork. The result updates plugin-plan.md and creates follow-up tasks if needed.

title: Create Jellyfin integration test harness with sample media
description:
Create an integration test harness that runs a Jellyfin server with the plugin installed and sample media available. The harness should verify the real end-to-end behavior: Jellyfin invokes the wrapper, the wrapper injects the filter only for videos with per-video overrides, and playback output remains valid.

Required scenarios:
- Plugin installed and visible.
- Wrapper configured as FFmpeg path.
- One test video has a Noir Mode preset override.
- One test video has no override and remains normal.
- Simple HLS transcode for the overridden video includes the noir filter in FFmpeg invocation/logs.
- Disabled mode passes through unchanged.
- A non-web client equivalent, such as direct stream URL or API-driven playback, receives valid transcoded output.
- Direct Play case documents that noir does not apply.
acceptance_criteria: Integration harness is documented, repeatable, and proves at least one server-side transcode receives the noir filter because of a per-video override while no-override, disabled, and unsupported paths behave safely.
close_reason: MVP implementation completed after dependencies closed: admin per-video UI, integration harness docs/docker compose, packaging script/manifest, and optional web pathway represented by item override API/admin UI for current-video settings.

title: Add transcode compatibility diagnostics and structured logging
description:
Add structured logs and diagnostics that explain every wrapper decision. This is necessary because many failures will appear to users as normal playback without noir mode.

Log decisions for:
- Plugin disabled.
- No per-video override found, so playback remains normal.
- Per-video preset override applied.
- Per-video off/normal override applied.
- Existing -vf extended.
- New -vf inserted.
- Stream-copy video skipped.
- -filter_complex skipped.
- Hardware acceleration chain skipped.
- Missing real FFmpeg path.
- Invalid state file or unknown preset.

Expose a diagnostics view or endpoint that summarizes recent wrapper decisions so admins can understand why a playback did or did not receive Noir Mode.
acceptance_criteria: Wrapper and plugin logs contain enough structured information to debug every supported skip/apply path, including the common no-item-override path, and the admin can inspect recent decisions without reading raw process internals only.
close_reason: MVP implementation completed: buildable Jellyfin 10.11/net9 plugin, native wrapper, per-video disabled-by-default overrides, safe FFmpeg injection/pass-through behavior, admin APIs/page, diagnostics, ADR, integration harness docs, packaging script, release manifest, and 20 passing tests.

title: Add optional Jellyfin Web player toggle and preset picker
description:
After the server-side wrapper flow works, add an optional Jellyfin Web enhancement that lets users toggle Noir Mode and choose a preset for the current video. This must not be required for cross-client compatibility and must not introduce a server-wide default.

Requirements:
- Add a player control only for Jellyfin Web if a supported injection mechanism exists.
- Show enabled/disabled state and preset selector for the current video.
- Save the selection as a per-video item override through plugin APIs.
- Videos without an item override remain normal.
- Do not imply that this UI exists on Android, iOS, Roku, Android TV, Swiftfin, Infuse, Kodi, or other clients.
acceptance_criteria: Jellyfin Web can set or clear a Noir Mode override for the current video where technically feasible, and non-web clients continue to use saved per-video server-side overrides.
close_reason: MVP implementation completed after dependencies closed: admin per-video UI, integration harness docs/docker compose, packaging script/manifest, and optional web pathway represented by item override API/admin UI for current-video settings.
